correctness.rationale: The structural condition is correct. The only distance-two pairs are pairs in the same non-singleton part \(V_i\), and their common neighborhood is exactly \(V(G)\setminus V_i\). Hence a set \(X\) is total mutual-visible exactly when its complement \(Y\) meets \(V(G)\setminus V_i\) for every non-singleton part, equivalently \(Y\not\subseteq V_i\) for every such part. Weighted inclusion-exclusion over the disjoint partite classes gives the polynomial. Inclusion-minimal admissible complements are exactly a singleton from a singleton part or, when at least two non-singleton parts exist, a two-set meeting two distinct such parts. The resulting maximal-set counts and lower number follow. A fresh independent check for profile \((2,2,1)\) gave coefficient vector \((1,5,10,8,1,0)\), agreeing with the formula; the frozen verifier checks every multipartite isomorphism type through order nine.

originality.rationale: Bujtás--Klavžar--Tian prove the stronger all-graph characterization: \(X\) is total mutual-visible iff for every distance-two pair \(u,v\), the common neighborhood \(N(u)\cap N(v)\) is not contained in \(X\). Specializing this theorem to a complete multipartite graph immediately gives the submitted complement condition because same-part pairs are the only distance-two pairs and have common neighborhood \(V\setminus V_i\). Their Proposition 3.2 already computes the total visibility polynomial for balanced complete bipartite graphs and explicitly notes that general \(K_{m,n}\) is obtained similarly. After the general criterion, the arbitrary-multipartite formula is one inclusion-exclusion step and the maximal-set theorem is the elementary classification of inclusion-minimal complements satisfying that condition.

final_claim: For a connected complete multipartite graph, the total visibility polynomial is obtained by excluding complements contained in one non-singleton part; the same complement condition classifies all maximal total mutual-visibility sets and yields the stated three-case lower total mutual-visibility number and maximal-set count.
